heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

MADIUN REGENCY GOVERNMENT

COPY

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim.
6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
1. Respect for the rights of victims.
2. Justice and gender equality.
3. Non-discrimination.
4. Best interests of the victim.
5. Respect for the rights of women and children.

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The purpose of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and in the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public sphere.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights relating to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The organization of services for victims is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

PPT managers are obliged to organize services in accordance with the service principles as referred to in Article 9.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

ASSISTANCE

Article 11

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with PPT.

CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:

Article 13

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY

NUMBER 5 OF 2008 CONCERNING ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's territory.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect maintained in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 1

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of victims' rights.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is action based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 4

What is meant by receiving protection is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both governmental and non-governmental.

Receiving information about the location of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and the development of case handling.

What is meant by integrated services are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by continuous handling is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including the restoration of their good name.

heading: Article 5
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MADIUN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 5

What is meant by receiving psychological and legal assistance at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
